solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Norm hit by Penny gets a shiner

blocks.note: to lam is to thrash or hit
p is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: Someone named Norm is punched by Penny and ends up with a black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shiner' looks like a black eye; here it is something that shines. 'Hit by Penny' reads as the attack, but it is two pieces joined.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall floor-standing household lamp gives off light, so it is jokingly a thing that shines.

clue.text: Destroyed old tape of swimmer

indicators.note: destroyed things are wrecked and broken apart, ready to be rebuilt differently

explanation.surface: A ruined vintage video recording of an Olympic swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is a frog's larva, which swims in ponds with its tail.

clue.text: Write article in support of new drug as a pain reliever

indicators.note: in a down answer a support lies underneath, so these pieces go below the others

explanation.surface: A journalist writes a piece backing a new painkilling medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'in support of' puts the first pieces underneath the later ones, so they come last.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepenthe was a drug in Homer that banished grief, so anything bringing forgetfulness of sorrow.

clue.text: Further letters found in Stendhal’s office

indicators.note: the run of letters is discovered sitting inside the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of the novelist's name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: More correspondence turns up in the French novelist Stendhal's study.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and further both serve as adverbs meaning in addition or besides.

clue.text: Soldiers touring area after princess becomes lost

indicators.note: a tour goes all round a place, so one word encircles the letter

explanation.surface: Troops guarding a region, following a royal, go missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that disappears vanishes from sight, which is to say it is lost.

clue.text: A European king’s rejected suit

indicators.note: what is rejected is thrown out, so that letter leaves the word

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A continental monarch has had his lawsuit thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like a lawsuit, but it is the verb, as in 'that date suits me'.
explanation.definitionFit: When food or a plan agrees with you it suits you, a verb sense of fitting.

clue.text: Criticise a revolutionary’s swagger

blocks.note: to pan a show is to slate it

explanation.surface: Mocking a rebel's arrogant strut.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence of style, close to a stylish swagger.

clue.text: Angry converts rail about nothing being open to question

indicators.note: angry people are worked up and agitated, so the letters are thrown about
about means around, so these letters go round the other one

explanation.surface: Furious new believers rant about nothing, their faith being doubtful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail' here is a verb, to complain bitterly, but it is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A controversial matter provokes disagreement, so it is disputed and open to debate.

clue.text: Slide headlong

blocks.note: first meaning: a tall spiral fairground slide
second meaning: in a disorderly, hurried rush

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as one phrase, someone sliding head first; they are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a fairground ride you slide down; the adverb means in confused haste.

clue.text: Correct for the most part to block work of legendary riddle solver

indicators.note: most but not all of the word is used, so its final letter is lost
something that blocks sits inside and fills the gap in another word

blocks.note: to correct a text is to edit it; drop the last letter
an opus is a work, especially of music

explanation.surface: Mostly-right advice on stopping a piece of work, oddly linked to a mythical riddler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correct' looks like an adjective but is the verb, meaning to amend a text.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Oedipus answered the Sphinx's riddle about the creature walking on four, two and three legs.

clue.text: Bound to have time at the end for a gin

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word is wanted, the one at its end

blocks.note: to bound is to leap or spring

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to take time over a gin and tonic at the end of the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' is not the drink but a trap, and 'Bound to' is not obligation but a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A springe is a snare for small game, and gin is an old word for such a trap.

clue.text: Undecided over Henry’s source of discomfort

indicators.note: one word lies over and around the other, covering it on both sides

blocks.note: someone undecided is torn between choices
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Indecision about a man named Henry is causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry is not a name but the unit of inductance, symbol H.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn in one's side is an idiom for a persistent irritation or annoyance.

clue.text: Run away after drug is found in punch

blocks.note: an upper is a stimulant drug
to cut and run, or simply cut, is to run off

explanation.surface: Someone flees after narcotics turn up in the party punch bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the running-away piece second. 'Punch' looks like the drink, but it is a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: An uppercut is a boxing blow swung upwards to the opponent's chin.

clue.text: Lower junior to tidy home

blocks.note: someone junior to another is under them

explanation.surface: A junior is ordered to bring down the tidying at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' looks like a verb but it is a comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something underneath is below, in a lower position than something else.

clue.text: Generous to provide free worker education

blocks.note: free of charge or restriction, open
a hand is a manual worker, as on a farm

explanation.surface: A generous scheme offers free schooling to workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone open-handed gives freely, a synonym for liberal or bountiful.

clue.text: Earl entering very much in awe

indicators.note: a letter that enters goes inside the other word

blocks.note: far better means very much better
E is the abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: An earl walks in, and everyone is deeply impressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe is reverential wonder mixed with dread, close to fear.

clue.text: Irregular soldiers engaged in dubious banter

indicators.note: troops engaged in an action are inside it, so these letters go within
something dubious is suspect and not straight, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Irregular troops trade questionable jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irregular' looks like an adjective for the soldiers, as in irregular troops, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrant means departing from the normal or expected, hence irregular or deviant.

clue.text: Wife leaves club with creep

indicators.note: the letter departs from the word and is no longer part of it

blocks.note: w is the abbreviation for wife
a wedge is a golf club

explanation.surface: A wife walks out of a nightclub accompanied by an unpleasant man.
explanation.walkthrough: The club is a golf wedge, not a nightclub; and creep is a verb, not a nasty person.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge forward is to inch or move slowly and carefully, as one creeps.

clue.text: American in danger transferred from island

indicators.note: things transferred are moved about to new positions

explanation.surface: A US citizen at risk is evacuated from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1983 US invasion of Grenada evacuated Americans, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenada is a Caribbean island nation in the Windward Islands.

clue.text: Courage to overcome grief

blocks.note: to have heart is to have courage
to break an opponent or a resistance is to overcome it

explanation.surface: Bravery is needed to get over a bereavement.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartbreak is overwhelming sorrow or distress, a synonym for grief.

clue.text: Put into words by Swift

blocks.note: first meaning: to state or articulate
second meaning: fast, as of a train or delivery

explanation.surface: Something written down by the satirist Jonathan Swift.
explanation.walkthrough: Swift looks like the author of Gulliver's Travels, but it means fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to state in speech or writing; the adjective means high-speed, as an express train.

clue.text: Went to stop Carol from going too fast

indicators.note: a plug stops a gap, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: to carol is to sing joyfully
to go is slang for to urinate

explanation.surface: Someone pulled over to prevent a woman called Carol driving above the limit.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol is a verb here, not a woman; 'went' is the childish sense of going to the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Speeding is exceeding a limit, especially driving faster than the law allows.

clue.text: Girl initially needing help comes up with answer

indicators.note: initially points to the very first letter of the word
in a down answer, coming up means reading from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A girl who needs assistance at first turns up with a solution.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana is a woman's given name, so a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: King reportedly returned without page in disgust

indicators.note: what is reported is what people say, so the word is taken by its sound
something returned goes back the way it came, so it is read from the end
without in its old sense means outside, so these letters go round the other

blocks.note: Shakespeare's King Lear, whose name is said the same as a lecherous look
p is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A monarch is said to have come back without his attendant boy, appalled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it has its old sense of outside, as in the hymn 'a green hill far away, without a city wall'.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel is to disgust or revolt, a verb sense alongside driving back.

clue.text: Left in fairy queen’s back ointment

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the other word
back means the queen's name is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: Queen Mab, the fairy queen in Romeo and Juliet

explanation.surface: Something abandoned in the fairy queen's rear salve.
explanation.definitionFit: Balm is a soothing fragrant preparation rubbed on skin, a salve.

clue.text: A president loses over backing the French state

indicators.note: the president's name gives up a letter and goes without it
backing means coming behind in support, so this piece follows the one before it

blocks.note: o is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A president loses ground after French opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' is a cricket term, abbreviated O; an over is six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Deep South.

clue.text: Made to diversify in excellent place of learning

indicators.note: to diversify is to vary, so the letters take on a varied order
one set of letters is put inside the other word

explanation.surface: A first-rate institution was forced to broaden its range.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe means the academic world, the environment of universities and scholarship.

clue.text: Tease hit man unsettled by a curse

indicators.note: unsettled things are disturbed and knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A contract killer is rattled by being mocked and then hexed.
explanation.definitionFit: To anathematise is formally to curse or denounce, originally by excommunication.
